resources.heading: Free up memory
resources.lead: Running projects, largest first. Nothing stops until you choose.
resources.vmLine: Containers use {used} of the {total} Docker Desktop VM ({pct}%) · {cpus} CPUs. Running projects, largest first. Nothing stops until you choose.
resources.footnote: Snapshot from `docker stats`, measured only when you click Measure RAM/CPU (here or on the Container RAM card). Low CPU does not mean a project is unused, so nothing is marked idle here.

usedBy.one: Running {projects} joins its network: stopping it may break it.
usedBy.other: Running {projects} join its network: stopping it may break them.

resources.measuring: Measuring… docker stats takes about 2 seconds.
resources.notMeasured: Not measured yet. Click Measure RAM/CPU to see which projects use the most memory (docker stats, about 2 seconds).

advisor.heading: Health & resource advisor
advisor.scoreTitle: Starts at 100. Each problem below deducts a fixed number of points, listed under How the score works.
advisor.observing: To find idle projects, measure RAM/CPU again in about {minutes} min: a project is idle when it had no traffic and CPU under 1% between two measurements at least {idle} min apart.
advisor.capped: Counted in this rule's cap: no extra points deducted.

rule.memoryNearLimit: Container at 90%+ of its memory limit
rule.partialDown: Service down while its project runs
rule.oomPast: Out of memory in the last run

p.missingNetwork: {project} needs network {network}, which no longer exists
p.vmMemory: Containers use {used} of the {total} Docker VM ({pct}%)

f.engine: Start Docker Desktop and wait until it is running, then re-check.
f.crashloop: Open its log to see why it exits; it often waits for a service that is stopped.
f.unhealthy: Open its log: the healthcheck fails.
f.startFailed: Docker's reason is shown below; fix it, then start the project again.
f.oom: Give the service more memory (mem_limit in Compose or the Docker Desktop VM size) or reduce its usage.
f.partialDown: Start the project to bring the stopped service back.
f.missingNetwork: Start the project that creates the network, or Up this project.
f.portConflict: Stop the container or process that holds the port, or change the port in Compose.
f.memoryNearLimit: Raise its mem_limit in Compose or reduce its usage before it gets killed.
f.hostPressure: Stop projects you don't need or lower the Docker Desktop memory limit.
f.vmMemory: Stop projects you don't need, or give the Docker Desktop VM more memory (Settings → Resources).

r.pruneCacheOld: Clean build cache unused for 30+ days

why.idle: {project}: no network traffic and CPU under 1% for {minutes} min.
why.vm: Containers use {pct}% of the Docker VM memory.
why.cache: Only slows the next image build; no project data is touched.
why.dangling: Untagged leftovers of rebuilt images that no container uses.
why.images: You would pull or rebuild them again. Compare in Docker Desktop → Images → Unused.
why.volumes: They may hold database data, so they are never removed automatically. Back up before removing one by hand.

risk.kept: Containers and volumes are kept; start them again any time.
risk.active: Still in use: stopping it interrupts your work.
risk.unknownActivity: Not measured long enough to know whether it is in use: measure RAM/CPU again later to find out.

keep.active: In use: network traffic or CPU seen
keep.observing: Needs a second measurement to judge

advisor.notAnalyzed: Click Check, Measure or Analyze on the cards above; the results appear here. Nothing runs until you click.
advisor.stale: projects changed since then: click ↻ in each box to update
advisor.healthEmpty: Not checked yet: click Check on the Docker health card above. It reads container states, this Mac's memory pressure and port conflicts (about half a second).
advisor.wasteEmpty: Click Measure on the Container RAM card or Analyze on the Reclaimable disk card above to see where resources are wasted.
advisor.actionsEmpty: Click Check, Measure or Analyze on the cards above to get suggestions.

ports.heading: Ports
ports.desc: Host ports held by containers (running, or reserved by stopped ones) and by other processes on this Mac. Pick free ones for a new project.
ports.footnote: Reserved = a stopped container will need this port when it starts again; taking it for a new project makes that start fail. Ports from 49152 up are assigned at random by macOS and are never suggested. Root-owned listeners are not listed but are caught by Check.
ports.lanTitle: Reachable from other machines on your network
ports.invisibleHolder: Something not visible to lsof answers on this port
ports.resultFree: free: nothing holds or reserves it.
ports.invisibleHolderLong: a process not visible to lsof (root?) that answers on this port

highSummary.one: High ports held by other apps ({count}): usually random, they change when the app restarts
highSummary.other: High ports held by other apps ({count}): usually random, they change when the app restarts

ports.highSummaryInitial: High ports held by other apps

note.cannotStart: Cannot start while {holder} holds this port.
note.alsoReserved: Also reserved by stopped {containers}: only one can run at a time.

disk.heading: Disk cleanup
disk.desc: Runs `docker system df -v` on demand (a few seconds). This tool never deletes anything: copy a command if you decide to clean.
disk.analyzing: Analyzing… docker system df -v usually takes a few seconds.
disk.volumesFold: Largest volumes not used by any container ({count} shown)
disk.inspectFoot: Inspect one with `docker volume inspect <name>`. Back up before removing anything by hand.
disk.measured: Measured {time} with docker system df -v. Figures match Docker's own RECLAIMABLE column.

ctx.anonymous: Anonymous volume: often a database image VOLUME left behind by a removed container
ctx.projectAlive: Project still has containers: maybe data of a removed service
ctx.leftover: Project has no containers left: likely a leftover, check before removing

row.unusedVolumes: Volumes not used by any container

note.buildCache: Only speeds up image builds. Removing it makes the next build slower; no project data is touched.
note.dangling: Untagged leftovers of rebuilt images that no container uses.
note.unusedImages: Tagged images that no container uses. Removing one means pulling or rebuilding it again. Review them in Docker Desktop → Images → Unused.
note.stoppedContainers: Removing a container loses its log and files written outside volumes. Use Down on projects you no longer need.
note.unusedVolumes: May contain database or upload data. This tool never removes volumes; back up before removing one by hand.

noErrors.other: No error-looking lines in the last {count} lines.

noteErrors.other: {shown} of {total} lines matching error keywords, oldest first

footer.text: Docker Dev Manager · localhost only · Stop preserves volumes · Down removes Compose containers and networks

exit.c127: Command not found in the image.

preflight.portTakenStandalone: Port {port} needed by {service} is taken by running container {container} (not in a Compose project). Stop it first or change the port.

preflight.noContainersManaged: No containers exist yet. Use Up in Details to create them.

preflight.providerStopped: Joins network {networks} of project {project}, which is not running: services it provides (database, cache, proxy…) stay unreachable until it starts.

dependents.one: Running {projects} joins this project's network ({networks}): its access to this project's services will break.
dependents.other: Running {projects} join this project's network ({networks}): their access to this project's services will break.

dependentsDown.one: Running {projects} joins this project's network ({networks}): Down removes that network and its access to this project's services will break.
dependentsDown.other: Running {projects} join this project's network ({networks}): Down removes that network and their access to this project's services will break.

preflight.downInfo: Down removes the Compose containers and networks of this project. Named volumes are kept.
preflight.upNeedsImport: Up is only available for imported projects: it needs the exact Compose file.
preflight.externalNetwork: External network "{network}" does not exist. Start the project that creates it first.
preflight.upRecreates: Up creates missing containers and recreates any whose configuration changed.

containerNeeds.one: {container} depends on {services}, which is not running: start it first, or {container} may fail to start.
containerNeeds.other: {container} depends on {services}, which are not running: start them first, or {container} may fail to start.

containerDependents.one: {services} depends on {container}: it keeps running but may fail until {container} is back.
containerDependents.other: {services} depend on {container}: they keep running but may fail until {container} is back.

containerSharedNetwork.one: Running project {projects} uses network {networks}, which this container is on, and may rely on it.
containerSharedNetwork.other: Running projects {projects} use network {networks}, which this container is on, and may rely on it.
